title: Teenager shot dead by off-duty officer was Iranian émigré
article: A person shot dead by a policeman in a Vancouver suburb this week was an 18-year-old who came to Canada from Iran two years ago, a police spokesman said yesterday.
Keyvan Tabesh was killed as he ran toward a police officer waving a machete, Constable Brian Soles, of the Port Moody police department, said in an interview.
Moments earlier, Mr. Tabesh had used the machete to rip into the side of a vehicle that had blocked his way on the road.
Neither his mother nor father were available for interviews yesterday. However, members of the Iranian community in Vancouver raised questions about the fatal shooting.
"Things may not be as black and white as \[the police\] say," said Ramin Mahjouri, editor of Paivand, an Iranian paper published twice weekly in Vancouver.
Family members have apparently been told that the police officer who shot Mr. Tabesh was off duty, he said. Police have said the officer was not in uniform and was not driving a marked police car.
Mr. Mahjouri questioned whether Mr. Tabesh would have known that a police officer was following him.
Constable Soles said police had had contact with Mr. Tabesh before the shooting but that he did not have a criminal record. The constable would not elaborate.

Mr. Mahjouri said he has been told that Mr. Tabesh was knifed in a fight a few weeks after he arrived in Canada, two years ago. Otherwise, he has been described as "a quiet, nice guy." However, he might have been drinking on the night of the fatal incident, he added.

The death has led to an internal investigation into police conduct, a homicide investigation into the death and a coroner's inquest. An autopsy was done yesterday, and results were to be available later this week.
Constable Soles said the officer, who has not yet been publicly identified, spotted Mr. Tabesh's car after hearing a call on police radio for assistance with a road-rage incident.

The officer followed the car to a dead end. Mr. Tabesh and a passenger in his car jumped out and started running toward the policeman, who had stopped just metres away. Constable Soles said the officer fired his gun when he felt he was under attack.
Investigators are still piecing together exactly what happened, he added. So far, they have found five spent casings, including one from a bullet that was believed to have killed Mr. Tabesh.

Statements to police support preliminary findings that Mr. Tabesh was killed as he ran at the police officer with the machete raised to strike, Constable Soles said. "There may be an issue about whether the police officer identified himself," he said. "He has a responsibility to do it, if he is able to."

In any case, Mr. Tabesh was about to attack someone, he added. "If a mistake was made, it is certainly clear that it was \[Mr. Tabesh and the unnamed passenger in the car\] that made it," Constable Soles said.
